issue.description:
The plan's architecture states every utility is a leaf sharing nothing with its siblings ('no cross-utility runtime dependency'), and check-structure.py enforces this by rejecting symlinks and runtime references into a sibling utility. But Phase 3b (util-50917f2f) and the dependency definition (util-a80ea021) make org-rule-guard delegate its credential rule to agent-secrets' credential-guard — exactly the cross-utility reference shape the plan and the checker reject. Nothing in the documented contract defines a sanctioned composition mechanism: no install-time bundling model (org-rule-guard's install.sh copies a pinned credential-guard into its own installed layout), no declared-exception list the checker honors, and no statement of how the delegation satisfies or amends the leaf rule. As written, the moment Phase 3b lands it fails the CI layout gate on every push, or the delegation is implemented in a way the checker silently misses and the rule doesn't fire at runtime. To close: (1) decide the sanctioned mechanism — bundled copy with a version reference vs. a narrowly declared exception in the checker — and record it in docs/plan/plan.md and both utilities' READMEs; (2) extend check-structure.py to accept exactly that mechanism, keeping the blanket rejection for undeclared cross-utility references, with regression tests added to the suite called for by util-3f7e5c97; (3) record the decision as a blocking/related relationship to util-a80ea021 and util-50917f2f rather than expanding either bead past its acceptance boundary.

Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 3 (a). Companion to NEEDLE plan section 4.4 (operator-side loop).

## Why
The org-wide PreToolUse guard at ~/.claude/hooks/org-rule-guard.py (332 lines, six rules) has exactly
one output path: the deny JSON on stdout. Nothing records which rule fired, in which repo, how often.
The enforcement layer emits no learning signal, so CLAUDE.md prose cannot be tuned against evidence.

## Task
1. Create utilities/org-rule-guard/ as a leaf: hooks/org-rule-guard.py (ported from the live hook,
   same six rules, same fail-open contract), hooks/test_org_rule_guard.py (one allow and one deny
   fixture per rule, built at runtime so no rule-triggering literal sits in the test file), install.sh
   (idempotent copy into ~/.claude/hooks/; edits settings.json only with --wire), README.md, VERSION.
2. On every deny, append one JSON line to ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/org-rule-guard/denials.jsonl:
   ts (UTC ISO-8601), rule_id (stable slug), tool, cwd, session_id (from the hook input if present), and
   a redacted 80-char fragment of what matched. For the credential rule the fragment is the pattern
   name only; never a value. Directory mode 700. Logging failures never change the decision.
3. README: log format plus a jq recipe for "denials by rule_id, last 7 days".

## Acceptance
- Test suite passes against both the live hook and the ported copy on the same fixtures.
- A deny writes exactly one line; an allow writes nothing.
- install.sh without --wire does not touch ~/.claude/settings.json or overwrite an existing hook file.
